content.title: About
content.content: Bologna is a cooked sausage made from beef and pork, seasoned with spices, garlic, and sometimes wine. Traditionally it is formed into a large loaf that is sliced thinly. The product has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Bologna” comes from the Italian city of Bologna, where a similar sausage was first produced in the 19th century.
The classic recipe uses only meat, salt, spices and occasionally dry wine; no artificial flavorings are added.
Bologna is often served cold as a sliced deli meat on sandwiches, in salads, and on charcuterie boards.
Traditional preparation involves long, low‑temperature cooking, which keeps the sausage juicy.
In some countries Bologna is used as a base for hot dishes such as pasta sauces or casseroles.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Bologna provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to normal immune system function.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugar.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Bologna is salty, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some versions contain nitrite salts, which may be undesirable in excess.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare individuals allergic to beef or pork may react to Bologna.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While not as calorie‑dense as some sausages, it should still be eaten in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bologna can be enjoyed cold as sliced deli meat, added to sandwiches, salads, pasta dishes, or used in hot preparations such as casseroles. For a softer flavor it is sometimes lightly warmed in a pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Bologna in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. Once opened, it is best consumed within 5–7 days. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 2 months.
